February 2022 · Society

Why SeaBrick is a nonprofit

SeaBrick Society was incorporated under the Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act in February 2022, with a single stated purpose: to promote innovation and standards around environmentally sustainable marine infrastructure building materials.

When the first SeaBrick drawings were being made in late 2021, the question of who should own the idea came up almost immediately. A floating, interlocking brick is only useful if lots of people can build with it, test it, improve it and trust it. That argues for a steward whose job is the standard, not the sale.

So on 17 February 2022, SeaBrick Society was incorporated under the Canada Not-for-profit Corporations Act. Its articles state one purpose:

To promote innovation and standards around environmentally sustainable marine infrastructure building materials.

The articles also say the corporation is carried on without the purpose of gain for its members, that any profits must be used to further its purposes, that directors serve without remuneration, and that if the Society is ever wound up its remaining property goes to qualified donees. In March 2022 it was also registered in British Columbia, where it is based.

What the Society does, and does not do

The Society holds the research direction, the public record of what has been tried, and the standards work: what a SeaBrick should be, how it should connect, how it should be tested. Commercial development, fundraising for manufacturing and product sales have been carried by related companies rather than by the Society itself. The Society does not sell bricks, does not take investment and does not pay dividends.

It is worth being precise about one more thing. SeaBrick Society is a federally incorporated not-for-profit corporation. It is not a registered charity, and it does not issue charitable tax receipts.

Why that matters for the work

Floating infrastructure for a changing coastline is a long project. Materials take years to qualify for marine use. Standards take longer still. A nonprofit can keep that work going across changes in funding, partners and even products, and it can publish what it learns, including what did not work. That is the role this website is built around.
